title: The Air Navigation (Restriction of Flying) (Portmoak, Perth and Kinross) (Emergency) Regulations 2026
summary: These Regulations impose restrictions of an emergency nature on flying in the area specified in the Schedule. They are intended to be of temporary duration and will be revoked as soon as the emergency in question has passed.

title: The Financial Services and Markets Act 2000 (Cryptoassets) (Miscellaneous Amendments) Regulations 2026
summary: These Regulations amend and add to the regulatory regime for certain cryptoasset activities pursuant to powers conferred by the Financial Services and Markets Act 2000 (c. 8) (“the Act”).

title: The Individual Savings Account (Amendment and Revocation) Regulations 2026
summary: These Regulations amend the Individual Savings Accounts Regulations 1998 (“the principal Regulations”) and the Individual Savings Account (Amendment) Regulations 2025, and revoke the Individual Savings Account (Amendment) (No. 2) Regulations 2026.

title: The Value Added Tax (Drugs and Medicines) (Health and Welfare) Order 2026
summary: This Order, which comes into force on 10th December 2026, makes amendments to Group 12 of Schedule 8 (“Group 12”) and Group 7 of Schedule 9 (“Group 7”) to the Value Added Tax Act 1994 (“VATA”). Group 12 zero-rates supplies of drugs, medicines and aids for the disabled. Group 7 exempts specified supplies of health and welfare from value added tax (“VAT”).

title: The Air Navigation (Restriction of Flying) (Loch Goil) Regulations 2026
The Financial Services and Markets Act 2023 (Addition of Relevant Enactments) Regulations 2026
summary: These Regulations add to the list of “relevant enactments” for the purposes of sections 13 to 17 of the Financial Services and Markets Act 2023 (c. 29) (“the Act”). Under section 13 of the Act, the Treasury may make regulations (an “FMI sandbox”) which may modify the effect or application of such relevant enactments for the purpose of testing the efficiency or effectiveness of new technologies or practices in the carrying on of financial markets infrastructure activities. The effect is to include new relevant enactments within the list at section 17(3) of the Act so that these enactments can be modified by future or existing FMI sandboxes.

title: The Air Navigation (Restriction of Flying) (Helicopter Flight) (No. 11) Regulations 2026
The Air Navigation (Restriction of Flying) (Specified Area) (Restricted Area EGR160) Regulations 2026
The Armed Forces (Amendment of Service Courts Rules) Rules 2026
summary: Under section 253A(2) of the Armed Forces Act 2006 (c. 52), inserted by section 6 of the Sentencing Act 2026 (c. 2), the court or commanding officer has a duty to make a statement in open court when passing sentence for a service offence if the court or officer is of the view that the offence involved domestic abuse carried out by the offender.

title: The Planning and Infrastructure Act 2025 (Commencement No. 5 and Transitional Provisions) Regulations 2026
summary: These Regulations bring into force two provisions in the Planning and Infrastructure Act 2025 (“the 2025 Act”). Regulation 2 brings into force sections 40(3) and 43 on 20th November 2026. Both provisions make amendments to the Transport and Works Act 1992. Regulation 3 makes transitional provision. It provides that section 40(3) applies to applications under section 1 or 3 of the Transport and Works Act 1992 made before these Regulations came into force only where a relevant notice has not yet been issued in respect of that application. The amendments made by section 43 do not apply to applications made before these Regulations come into force.

title: The Social Security (Non-Benefit Payments) Regulations 2026
summary: These Regulations specify which payments are a “non-benefit payment” under section 121DA(5) of the Social Security Administration Act 1992 (c. 5) (“the Administration Act”).

title: The Bank Levy (Definitions and Amendments) Regulations 2026
summary: These Regulations amend definitions in Schedule 19 to the Finance Act 2011 (“the Act”) and the Bank Levy (Loss Absorbing Instruments) Regulations 2020 in consequence of—

title: The Human Rights Act 1998 (Remedial) Order 2026
summary: This Order amends the Human Rights Act 1998 (“the HRA”) to address a finding of the European Court of Human Rights of a breach of Article 13 of the European Convention on Human Rights (“the Convention”) in the case of S.W. v United Kingdom (Application no. 87/18).

title: The Value Added Tax (Distance Selling) (Amendments) Regulations 2026
summary: These Regulations amend Schedules 9ZD, 9ZE and Part 3 of Schedule 9ZF to the Value Added Tax Act 1994 and come into force on 1st January 2027. They implement certain amendments made by Council Directive (EU) 2025/516 to Council Directive 2006/112/EC (“the VAT Directive”), pursuant to the United Kingdom’s obligations under the Windsor Framework.

title: The Critical Third Parties (Designation) (Amendment) Regulations 2026
summary: These Regulations designate BlackRock Financial Management, Inc., Bloomberg L.P., Bottomline Technologies Limited, Broadridge Financial Solutions Limited and Form3 UK Limited as critical third parties. The Regulations amend the Critical Third Parties (Designation) Regulations 2026 (S.I. 2026/777) to add the entities to the list of designated critical third parties.

title: The Traffic Orders and Notices (Provision of Digital Information) (England) Regulations 2026
summary: These Regulations make provision to require traffic regulation authorities in England to provide information to the Secretary of State about the traffic regulation measures that they make. The Secretary of State will, in turn, publish that data in open data format (available via https://www.gov.uk/guidance/digital-traffic-regulation-orders-d-tro-service) so that it can be used for the purposes set out in section 93(5) of the Automated Vehicles Act 2024 (c. 10) (“the 2024 Act”).

title: The Online Safety Act 2023 (Commencement No. 8) Regulations 2026
summary: These Regulations are the eighth commencement regulations made under the Online Safety Act 2023 (c. 50) (“the Act”). They bring into force section 75 of the Act which places duties on providers of Category 1, 2A and 2B services to set out their policies on disclosing information to the parents of deceased child users, have a dedicated helpline or section of the service (or similar means) for such parents, provide details about the relevant policies and procedures in their terms of service or a publicly available statement, and respond in a timely manner to requests for information. Section 75 also requires the providers to operate a complaints procedure in relation to these duties.

title: The Railways (Interoperability in Northern Ireland) (Convention on International Carriage by Rail) (Amendment) Regulations 2026
summary: These Regulations implement Directive (EU) 2016/797 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 11 May 2016 on the interoperability of the rail system within the European Union (O.J. No. L 138, 26.5.2016, p. 44) (the “2016 Directive”) for Northern Ireland, making technical provision for the placing on the market, putting into service and free movement of railway products. The 2016 Directive is a recast of Directive 2008/57/EC of the European Parliament and of the Council of 17 June 2008 (O.J. No. L 191, 18.7.2008, p. 1), which was transposed for Great Britain and Northern Ireland by way of the Railways (Interoperability) Regulations 2011 (S.I. 2011/3066). These Regulations replace that regime for Northern Ireland in line with the UK’s obligations pursuant to Article 5(4) and Annex II of the Windsor Framework.

title: The Electrical Safety Standards in the Private Rented Sector and Social Rented Sector (England) (Amendment) Regulations 2026
summary: These Regulations amend the Electrical Safety Standards in the Private Rented Sector and Social Rented Sector (England) Regulations 2020 (S.I. 2020/312) (“the Principal Regulations”).

title: The Hazards in Social Housing (Prescribed Requirements) (England) (Amendment) Regulations 2026
summary: These Regulations amend the Hazards in Social Housing (Prescribed Requirements) (England) Regulations 2025 (S.I. 2025/1042) (“the 2025 Regulations”), also known as “Awaab’s Law”, which prescribe requirements with which a landlord of social housing is required to comply by virtue of the covenant implied by section 10A(2) of the Landlord and Tenant Act 1985 (c. 70).
